rp.intro: A ministry incident calls for a political response. Compare support, a directive and dismissal before deciding.
rp.text.stuetzen: You take political responsibility: minister loyalty +6, resentment −6. Their coalition party gains support. Backing failure especially strengthens the opposition; the underlying situation is unchanged.
rp.text.zurueckpfeifen: Minister loyalty −5, resentment +8. Further unilateral administrative action is barred for 60 days; performance pressure lasts at least as long. Previous interventions and spending are not reversed.
rp.text.entlassen: The existing personnel procedure appoints an interim head. The ministry remains assigned to its party, but removing its minister still angers its leader. Onboarding and possible market reactions also apply.
rp.eigenGut: The minister acted unilaterally and slightly improved the ministry situation. The lack of coordination remains politically disputed.
rp.eigenSchlecht: The unilateral action cost money and worsened the ministry situation.
rp.stillstand: The ministry request received no policy response. Unresolved tasks are worsening the situation.
rp.sachfolge: {name}: {vor} → {nach}. Additional costs already booked: {bip}% of GDP.
rp.kontrolle: Directive in force until {datum}: no unilateral administrative initiatives. Unaddressed problems can still grow.
rp.nachfolger: {name} takes over · {partei}. Ability {faehigkeit}, loyalty {loyalitaet}. Onboarding until {datum} (performance factor ×0.75).
rp.opp.vorfall: {partei} demands an explanation of the ministry incident and government responsibility.
rp.opp.stuetzen: {partei} criticizes the government for shielding the minister.
rp.opp.zurueckpfeifen: {partei} acknowledges the directive but still demands a solution to the ministry problem.
rp.opp.entlassen: {partei} acknowledges the personnel consequence; substantive issues remain unresolved.
rp.personWechsel: {alt} leaves; {neu} takes over with their own profile. The predecessor remains in the former officials record and may later speak publicly.
rp.bruch: If support stays unchanged, {parteien} may leave on {datum}: government seats {vor} → {nach}; {fehlt} then missing for an absolute majority. Active leaders below 20 loyalty trigger the monthly check.
rp.keinBruch: This decision alone leaves no currently active coalition leader below 20 loyalty. Further crises and open promises can change that.
rp.grenze: These personnel decisions require no new parliamentary vote. Faction willingness affects future negotiations; government seats are lost only upon an actual exit. No promise or underlying problem is automatically resolved.
rp.historisch: Saved reactions at the time of each event. Later alliance changes do not rewrite these records.
rp.wechsel: The office holder has changed; this incident requires no decision about the successor.
rp.ueberholt: A newer incident involving the same minister replaced this open case.
rp.veraltet: The case or its conditions changed. Please review the current preview.
rp.kapital: The required {n} political capital is unavailable, including the allowed overdraft.
rp.erinnerung.stuetzen: The president publicly backed me after the ministry incident.
rp.erinnerung.zurueckpfeifen: After the ministry incident, the president barred unilateral action and ordered closer oversight.
rp.grund.kontrolle: The coalition demands coordinated government action.
rp.grund.versagen: The unresolved ministry conflict damages the shared government record.
rp.grund.rueckhalt: The party welcomes support for its minister.
rp.grund.mitverantwortung: Partners do not want to share responsibility for shielding failure.
rp.grund.massregelung: The party sees its minister publicly reprimanded.
rp.grund.entlassung: Dismissal of its own minister strains alliance support.
rp.grund.neustart: Other partners welcome the personnel consequence.
rp.grund.aufklaerung: The faction outside the coalition demands an explanation.
rp.grund.decken: The faction criticizes political backing for the minister.
rp.grund.verantwortung: The faction acknowledges a consequence without joining the government.
rp.auftrag: The agreed ministry target was missed at its deadline. The coalition demands a political response.
rp.entlassungZusatz: Open ministry incident: {n} additional attention. Dismissal triggers the same faction reactions as the incident card; existing promises remain open.
rp.kommissarisch: The interim appointment adds a performance factor of ×0.8 until a permanent successor is appointed.
rp.sachKosten: Extra costs already booked: {bip}% of GDP.
rp.grenzeTitel: What this decision does not change
